title: Mathematics Practice Test 2 - Mathematics - Conic Sections
subject: Mathematics

questions.q: The hyperbolas $\frac{x^2}{9} - \frac{y^2}{4} = 1$ and $\frac{y^2}{36} - \frac{x^2}{25} = 1$ are graphed in the standard $(x,y)$ coordinate plane. Which of the following equations is an ellipse that intersects all 4 vertices of the hyperbolas?
questions.explain: To find the vertices of the first hyperbola, set $y = 0$: $\frac{x^2}{9} = 1$, giving $x = \pm 3$. Thus, two vertices are $(3, 0)$ and $(-3, 0)$. To find the vertices of the second hyperbola, set $x = 0$: $\frac{y^2}{36} = 1$, giving $y = \pm 6$. The other two vertices are $(0, 6)$ and $(0, -6)$. An ellipse with center at $(0,0)$, x-intercepts at $\pm 3$, and y-intercepts at $\pm 6$ follows the form $\frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$. Substituting $a=3$ and $b=6$ results in the equation $\frac{x^2}{9} + \frac{y^2}{36} = 1$.
